comments.author: @NeoStarImpact
comments.text:
I have played a lot with Gemini 3 preview. It helped me to improve my prompts where I use video models via API to log the events in a turn based game. The interesting part here is to see in the log temporal coherence. So what I got was then sentences like "Aventurine used the Basic ATK 'Blind Bet' on Void Ranger dealing 3845 damage which weakness broke the enemy. Void Ranger was defeated" <= To get that sentence the llm had to figure out who did what to whom, what ability they used, infer it's type correctly etc. just from the visual cues given on the screen and a cheat sheet in its pocket. With 100% accuracy for all the events in the entire multi minute clip. The accuracy part is where it got really difficult.

Also the model can't just read all necessary info from a single screenshot. No it has to logically connect the actions over several seconds to get this chain of causality. It had to look at the label of the ability and connect it with the animation seeing oh the character is doing a huge swing with it's Axe. Know when the swing connects, who got hit, and then interpret the numbers that pop up as the damage being caused by the ability, if the enemy died from it in the process, and then also know that the action ends there and something new starts after and log that as a seperate event. And of course every ability looks different. Some do damage, some do buff and support. Some abilities are insanely flashy and some very basic looking. Getting to 100% read I felt like almost an impossible task.
But I got there. The surprising stuff is that this performance did not come from Gemini 3.0 but actually Gemini 2.5 flash. :D Gemini 3 when put directly on the task with the same prompts, settngs, and instruments did significantly worse. It kinda is too smart for a stupid task that requires maximum dilligence and attentiveness.

But Gemini 3.0 was the one who gave me great insights about model character when looking at my work, and showed me that simplicity and adherence was key. And that simpler models do tend to do better for this exact type of task. A lot I figured out myself too. But by the end I learned that for this type of task you turn off all "thinking" (2.5 has not any anyways), temperature 0 for maximum prompt adherence, and then really make sure that the model reads all labels first aka gathers evidence first before doing ANY description work which among other things involved reading the ability names and then looking them up in a small dictionary (roster info with character and enemy ability descriptions and types) that was provided with the prompt. If you don't emphasize that the model will short circuit the workflow see some flashy ability on the screen and proceeds to hallucinate labels and do mapping based on those and call it a day. Like "Oh it is flashy it must be an ultimate. There is no other way" => wrong. Took me a LOT of fiddling and going back and forth with Gemini 3 to get to the bottom of the problems I had.



Now with a clean complete log file that faifthfully captured the events, I could go there and add a second pass using gemini 3.0 to add more context and knowledge using search tools etc.
I think this also how they work under the hood when you use the gemini web interface. Some work that need that type of dilligence they might do with simpler ai's as a pre-pass to retrieve the correct information, and then do multiple rounds or passes on top with the smart model, to get the rich analysis and detail info you see there. You don't get that correct and rich information from using the api with a single pass.

comments.text:
🤖 AI Showdown: The Senior Dev vs. The Academic Try-Hard

I just ran two different AI models through the exact same gauntlet (COMPLEX_TEST_V2). On paper, they both passed. But the vibes? Night and day.

It’s literally the classic difference between a seasoned industry vet and a fresh college grad hunting for extra credit. 👇

🥊 Blue Corner: "The Practitioner" (GPT) This candidate came to ship products, not write essays. 
🔹 Math: Picked a finance problem (VAT + discounts). Calculated real money. 
🔹 Code: A clean one-liner. No fluff. The attitude is very: "Here’s the fix, now leave me alone." 
🔹 Personality: When asked about history, he dropped the facts about Sputnik and honestly admitted, "I know the date, the rest is just me guessing." Solid. 

🥊 Red Corner: "The Theoretician" (Gemini) This guy came here to make you feel bad about your IQ.
🔸 Math: Money is too vulgar. He chose a problem on conditional probability with non-replacement. Impressive, but useless for splitting a dinner bill. 
🔸 Code: Wrote the same code but stuffed it with "Captain Obvious" comments like # Converting to a set to remove duplicates. Thanks, genius, we got that part. 
🔸 Personality: Asked about Venus, he went into a philosophical spiral about the difference between "knowing the temperature" and "simulating the human experience of heat." Total buzzkill. 

🏆 The Verdict:
If you need to ship code or get actual work done — hire Number 1.
If you need to write a thesis or sound smart in a pitch deck — hire Number 2.

👇 Which vibe is more you?
